- SLOs: target p95 latency < 400ms for short prompts; embeddings for search are batched and less latency-sensitive.

Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up & benchmark — Redwood vs OpenAI/Anthropic

Sara — thanks for the numbers, that helps a lot. Attached is a short benchmarking note (PDF) and our model spreadsheet — high level summary below. I included comparisons vs: OpenAI (gpt-4o-ish/chat + embeddings), Anthropic (Claude chat + embeddings), and representative open-model hosts (Hugging Face inference + hosted LLM providers).

Executive summary (target $/1M tokens):
- Redwood (recommended config: quantized LLM variant + batching, prefix caching): $300–$900 / 1M tokens depending on committed tier and embedding mix.
  - With reserved/dedicated commit (12mo) and prefix caching for steady traffic: target $300–$400 / 1M tokens.
  - Self-serve hosted, on-demand (no commit): $700–$900 / 1M tokens.
- OpenAI (public list): ~ $1,000–$1,500 / 1M tokens for similar chat-capable model + embeddings (varies by model and context length).
- Anthropic: ~ $900–$1,300 / 1M tokens (chat model + embeddings).
- Open-model hosts (HF/other): wide range, typically $500–$1,200 / 1M tokens depending on model/quantization & infra; some cheaper for embeddings-only hosts but with higher latency and less reliability.

For Finex's profile (215M tokens/month + 80M embedding tokens):
- If you commit to a reserved tier (monthly committed tokens / capacity), we can target ~$320 / 1M tokens blended across chat+embedding usage. That maps to roughly $98k/month blended — but that's with a 12mo term and reservation (we can model different durations).
- If you need self-serve hosted only (no commit), we'd expect ~$700–900 / 1M tokens which would place your spend ~ $190k–$270k/month.

Key levers to lower unit cost:
- Reserved capacity (commits) — largest impact.
- Batching & prefix/KV caching — reduces per-token work for repeated prompts.
- Quantized model variants — small quality tradeoff, big cost wins.
- Routing non-critical traffic to cheaper model variants and reserving high-grade models for critical paths.

I put a recommended starter plan in the spreadsheet (attached) and a per-1M-token comparison table in the PDF. Links included to the HubSpot deal and a sample contract (DocuSign) if you want to move to a committed pilot.

Questions for you (to refine the proposal):
1) Would you consider a 6–12mo commit if the blended $/1M target is ~$320?
2) How much of the 215M monthly tokens are latency-sensitive chat vs background embedding/async workloads? (we assumed ~60% chat / 40% embeddings in the attached model)

If it helps, Aditya can run a quick 1-week load test with a quantized variant to validate latency/cost assumptions — would you like us to schedule that?

Best,
Marissa
Attachment: redwood_pricing_comparison.pdf; redwood_pricing_model.xlsx

Looping in a quick technical note — high level validation of Marissa's assumptions:

- The blended $/1M targets look achievable under dedicated/reserved capacity with quantized inference + KV caching. For 215M chat tokens + 80M embedding tokens we can optimize batching windows and put embeddings on a cheaper backend to lower blended cost.
- We recommend a short 7–10 day pilot (we can do a dedicated test cluster) to measure realized p95 and per-token CPU/GPU usage. That data will let us convert your CSV to a realistic $/1M estimate (we typically see 20–40% delta vs model-only spreadsheets once real traffic characteristics are applied).
